title: Transportation Security Inspector (Cyber)
location: Salt Lake City, Utah; Seattle, Washington; Phoenix, Arizona; Los Angeles, California; San Francisco, California; Denver, Colorado; Washington, District of Columbia; Miami, Florida; Atlanta, Georgia; Chicago, Illinois; Indianapolis, Indiana; New Orleans, Louisiana; Boston, Massachusetts; Minneapolis, Minnesota; Kansas City, Missouri; Albuquerque, New Mexico; New York, New York; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma; Portland, Oregon; Austin, Texas
description:
• This Transportation Security Inspector (Cyber) position is located at Surface Operations, West Region, Transportation Security Administration, Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Duties include but are not limited to: Provides technical expertise and support for criminal investigations related to alleged or suspected security threats and violation(s). Leads security assessments to identify unusual trends or actions that have the potential for developing into major security/safety problem(s) or violation(s). Performs comprehensive cybersecurity assessments utilizing the Cyber Security Evaluation Tool (CSET). Provides relevant training and education on utilizing this resource. Conducts inquiries and/or investigates surface transportation and pipeline security incidents, threats, violations or potential violations and other incidents as defined by the National Incident Management Systems (NIMS), or as directed by the respective Headquarters Directorate or appropriate authority. Prepares written reports to document regulatory and structured oversight (assessment) activities. Serves as an expert advisor/point of contact for surface transportation operations. Provides technical support for regulatory activities and monitors outreach programs within the pipeline, freight and passenger rail sectors. Develops or coordinates surface transportation security initiatives across the nation's pipeline transportation system that focus on security training, community outreach, security planning, intelligence and information sharing, security exercises, and operational detection and deterrence. Collaborates with other federal departments/agencies, the private sector, and other stakeholders to ensure that pipeline and freight and passenger rail cybersecurity risks are effectively managed, critical networks are protected, vulnerabilities are mitigated, cybersecurity threats are reduced and countered, and incidents are responded to in a timely and effective way. Plans, coordinates, and conducts all activities necessary for stakeholder engagement. Leads supporting efforts in the implementation of pipeline cyber measures that protect information technology and operational technology systems, including industry controls systems and other critical assets by safeguarding their confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Based on direction provided by TSA Headquarters, inputs data pertinent to incidents, inspections, investigations, assessments, training, exercises and outreaches into approved databases. Leads and/or participates in surface transportation related assessments to ensure the integrity of the applicable surface transportation security systems. Inspects and validates security processes, procedures, systems and equipment in connection with compliance inspections and vulnerability assessments. Conducts assessments to evaluate and analyze security posture and compliance.

Qualifications

To qualify for the SV-J Pay Band (equivalent to the GS-14), you must have one year of specialized experience at the SV-I or GS-13 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector. Specialized experience is defined as experience that has equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. Specialized experience is defined as: Conducting inspections and investigations; determining when enforcement action should be taken; Engaging in security assessments and evaluations of surface transportation security systems; Documenting the results to monitor compliance with policies, regulations, and agreements to standards; Identifying potential problem areas and deviation from prescribed standards. Credit for experience is given based on a 40-hour workweek. Part-time experience is credited on a part-time ratio, i.e., working 20 hours per week for two months equals one month of experience. No additional credit is given for overtime. National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. You must meet the qualification requirements for this position no later than the closing date of the vacancy announcement.
